audit.why: 49.82% over 1140 games is a genuine coin-flip lane, and the page already frames it as pattern management around her stun rather than a lane either side dominates.
audit.corrected: No difficulty-shape change proposed; corrections are mechanical.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike was justified by a 'Winter's Wrath percent-HP tick' that does not exist.
audit.why: Riot's text for Winter's Wrath is damage, a slow and Frost stacks — no percent max health component, and the kit carries no percentHealth flag. Her first-item strength is Frost Armor's free armour and MR stacked on a tank item, which blunts your physical damage.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[2].text and whys[5] around Frost Armor plus her first tank item. The chart rows themselves (Skill/Skill/Sejuani/Skill/Skill/Sejuani/Skill) still match their whys and the win rate, so no win[] flips proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the North grants immunity to slows and the page never mentions it, while repeatedly selling your E and Q slows as tools against her.
audit.why: Roar of the Slayer's slow and the Decimating Smash slow simply do not apply while Frost Armor is up, which is exactly when she opens on you. The armour shred still lands; the slow does not.
audit.corrected: Stated the slow immunity in whys[1] and late, and kept E framed as an armour-shred rather than a kiting tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown given for Arctic Assault, the ability the whole engage depends on.
audit.why: It is 18 seconds at rank 1 against your 10s Q — a missed or wasted Arctic Assault is the longest punish window in the lane.
audit.corrected: Added the 18s figure to whys[2] and early. Also gave Glacial Prison's 90s rank-3 cooldown in late.

audit.why: Nothing in the brief indicates a recent change to either kit on 26.15.

edits.before: Level 1 is a genuine coin flip — Sejuani's passive Frost stacks build on autos and her W Winter's Wrath tick, so she can set up a Permafrost stun without spending a single extra ability. Don't auto-trade freely; last-hit at Q range and let her show the Permafrost pattern before you commit. At level 2 your W-shield absorbs her Winter's Wrath damage and makes short trades cost her more, but she hits level 3 with the same Frost stacking threat. At level 3 she has her full kit too — Arctic Assault Q to close, W to stack Frost, E to stun — so her engage pattern is complete before yours. Respect that: charge Q from brush angles or behind a pushing wave where the telegraph is hidden, not in the open where she closes with Q and Permafrost fires before your knockup lands.
edits.after: Level 1 is a genuine coin flip — Frost stacks build on her autos and Winter's Wrath, so she sets up a Permafrost stun without spending an extra ability. Don't auto-trade freely; last-hit at Q range and let her show the Permafrost pattern first. At level 2 Soul Furnace absorbs Winter's Wrath and makes short trades cost her more, though Fury of the North's slow immunity means you cannot kite her out of one. At level 3 her engage is complete before yours — Arctic Assault closes on an 18-second cooldown, Winter's Wrath stacks, Permafrost stuns. So charge Q from brush or behind a pushing wave where the telegraph is hidden, and step up for free once that 18 seconds is running.

edits.before: Late game this matchup becomes about team value, not the 1v1. Your zombie passive makes every dive-in still punish — even dying into Sejuani's Glacial Prison R, your reanimated form can charge a knockup through her team while she's committing. Heartsteel's HP compound means you are an enormous frontline sponge by two items, but Sejuani's Winter's Wrath W percent-HP damage keeps ticking regardless of your total HP, so don't assume you out-stat her — you brawl as equals. The real win condition is landing Unstoppable Onslaught into their backline while Sejuani's Glacial Prison R is on cooldown, so she can't follow up; if you both ult at the same time you're just trading AoE CC and neither side dominates.
edits.after: Late game this matchup becomes about team value, not the 1v1. Your zombie passive makes every dive-in still punish — even dying into Glacial Prison, your reanimated form can charge a knockup through her team while she's committing. Heartsteel's HP compound makes you an enormous frontline sponge by two items, but Frost Armor hands her armour, magic resist and immunity to slows every time she is out of combat, so neither your E nor your Q slows her opener — you brawl as equals. The real win condition is landing Unstoppable Onslaught into their backline inside the 90 seconds Glacial Prison is down, so she cannot answer; ulting at the same time just trades AoE CC and settles nothing.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Use Arctic Assault' and 'Arctic Assaults' as probable wrong names — both are false positives; Arctic Assault is the correct Q name and the flagger is matching on case and verb inflection. The real defect in this matchup was invented: Winter's Wrath was described as a percent max health tick in three places (whys[5], spikes[2].text, late) and Riot's text has no percent health component at all. I could not verify from the kits whether Permafrost's stun interrupts a Decimating Smash charge or merely delays the release, so I left every claim about her stunning you mid-charge either untouched or rewritten to avoid asserting it.
